cues.text: Start. <break time='1s'/> I used to think I could manage AI permissions manually. You know... just check the code, run the agent. But... well, it's a losing game. <break time='1s'/> If you have ever had an agent hallucinate a delete command on your production database... <break time='500ms'/> You know that fear. It... it sits in your stomach. <break time='1.5s'/> This is why I built Nucleus. It's not just a tool. It is a local hypervisor that locks your files. Watch this. The agent tries to wipe my env file. <break time='1s'/> Blocked. Instantly. It logs the attempt... cryptographically. You have a receipt. You have control.

But security is boring if it doesn't have memory. <break time='1s'/> Most tools... they just block. But Nucleus? Nucleus *remembers*. See this 'Engram'? You teach the agent once. 'Never touch the secrets file.' 'Always use this design pattern.' It verifies this memory across every session. <break time='1.5s'/> Now... let's talk about the industry. Most Enterprise Compliance tools—like Splunk or Datadog Audit Trails—will charge you... well, twenty thousand dollars a year for this level of visibility. They call it 'Enterprise Security'. <break time='1s'/> I call it a tax. Nucleus gives you this audit trail for free. Locally. Because quite frankly... I do not trust the Cloud with my root keys.

And here is the beautiful part. It scales. Recursively. <break time='1s'/> I can mount my entire infrastructure. Stripe. Github. Postgres. The agent can see them. It can use them. But it cannot break the physics of the rules you set. <break time='1.5s'/> I can snap my fingers... and kill the entire swarm. <break time='2s'/> The local tool is free. It is yours. But if you want the Team Sync Feature and other advanced functions... <break time='1s'/> Comment SOVEREIGN below. Beta keys available. <break time='2s'/> Stay sovereign.
